newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to reconsider key rate this month - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to reconsider key rate this month - c.bank.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank will consider changing its 40-percent refinancing rate at the end of December, once the country makes payments for Treasury bills and foreign credits, bank chairman Viktor Yushchenko said late on Tuesday.

"Inflation of 1.2 percent in November creates proper conditions to change the rate, but we also know that the government must make large payments for Treasury bills, so we must be careful not to lose control of the money supply," he said.
The Finance Ministry must make more than 255 million hryvnia in T-bill payments on Wednesday.

Yushchenko did not say whether the rate, charged to banks borrowing money from the central bank, would be cut or raised but the bank has previously promised to lower it as inflation slows. Monthly inflation was 1.5 percent in October.
The rate was lowered to 40 percent on July 2 and was 105 percent at the beginning of the year.
